answer: Do not activate formal-gates for routine work unless the user explicitly requests the formal workflow.
Ask in plain language, name the user-visible choice, and explain why it matters.
An independent reviewer checks for the simplest sufficient solution before reviewing implementation details.
QA Design uses the confirmed requirement and stays blind to production implementation and developer explanations.
The worker adds every explicit new or untracked delivery path to the native VCS and never adds the whole worktree.
Add gates/*.md and reinstall; do not add a Go registry.
Send the exact task with the shared reviewer base once, the selected gate prompt once, and no prior findings.
Run selected QA Execution and every selected discovered gate in one parallel wave on the same current snapshot.
Continue every safe in-scope check, find the same defect pattern across the change, and report the complete related chain.
Use the immediate pre-repair-to-current native VCS comparison and decide INHERIT or RERUN for every prior passing selected discovered gate.
Rerun only the named gate using the complete base-to-current comparison, not only the repair diff.
Record RUNTIME_ERROR, distinct from reviewer FAIL, and require explicit user skip authorization before Seal may retain it without PASS.
Resume must preserve completed results, leave interrupted work PENDING, and dispatch only unfinished work.
Dispatch an independent QA Review with the confirmed requirement and complete candidate cases; development remains blocked until QA Review passes.
No-VCS mode is unsupported: do not copy files or create a custom snapshot or diff system.
Use reasoned main-agent Carry to inherit every previously passing selected result, including QA, only when the immediate repair diff proves all are unaffected; otherwise use independent Carry.
